item.title: Setting Up Hugo with GitHub Actions
item.description:
Once you’ve decided to move to GitHub Pages, the next question is: how do you automate the build and deployment?

Here’s the GitHub Actions workflow that makes it all work.

The Two-Repo Architecture

The setup uses two repositories:

  • Private repo (blogs): Your Hugo source, Markdown content, layouts, and config
  • Public repo (username.github.io): Compiled HTML only, auto-deployed

This keeps your drafts and source private while publishing only the final HTML.

item.title: Why I Moved My Blog to GitHub Pages
item.description:
Medium had a good run. But paywall friction for readers, and zero ownership of my own content, finally pushed me to make the move.

Here’s what the setup looks like and why I’m not going back.

The Problem with Medium

When you publish on Medium, you’re essentially renting space. Your content is behind their paywall mechanics, their algorithm decides distribution, and if Medium changes its terms — you’re along for the ride.
